Team — forwarding Quantico's legal questions. High level thoughts below; can you take the first draft of responses? I want to keep the tone firm but cooperative.

Liability cap: standard Redwood hosted SLA uses the greater of $250k or 6 months of recurring fees for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we have higher caps tied to committed ARR and available on a case-by-case basis with a contract amendment. Quantico is enterprise so we should offer the option of an increased cap tied to committed spend (e.g., 12 months of committed fees) but require approval by Sales Ops / Revenue.

IP: Redwood does not typically assign core product IP or model IP. For bespoke integrations or custom connectors built for a customer, we usually grant a perpetual, non-exclusive license to the customer; assignment only in rare strategic deals. If Quantico requires assignment, note that it will incur a one-time fee and need legal review around third-party model components.

Attachments to produce: 1) a short Exhibit Q redline that offers (i) alternate cap language referencing "12 months of committed fees up to $X" for dedicated commitments and (ii) clarified IP language that grants a perpetual license for custom deliverables and provides an assignment path for an additional fee. 2) a redlined order form.

Priom/Neha — can you draft the redline and an internal justification memo? I will review and then send to Quantico (cc'ing Sales Lead).

Priya

Priya — draft attached. Key points I added:

- Liability cap: proposed language (redline) that keeps the "greater of $250k or 6 months of fees" as default for Hosted, plus an optional higher-cap clause for Dedicated/Private with customer-elected increased cap equal to 12 months of committed fees subject to a signed Order Form Amendment and payment/commitment terms. - Indemnity: tightened our language around IP infringement to include indemnity capped by the liability cap and excluded to the extent third-party components/models contributed to the claim.

Hi Anna — thanks for the note and for flagging. Please find attached our proposed redlines and a short cover note that explains the approach. Summary below for faster review: 

1) Liability cap: Default (Hosted) remains the greater of $250,000 or 6 months of fees. For customers executing a Dedicated or Private order with a committed ARR/term, we will offer an optional increased cap equal to 12 months of committed fees (or a negotiated fixed cap) provided Quantico signs an Order Form Amendment committing to the associated spend. This addresses your "higher cap" ask while preserving standard exposures.

2) IP & deliverables: Redwood will continue to retain core product and model IP. For customer-funded bespoke deliverables (eg. custom connector code written exclusively for Quantico without third-party components), Redwood will offer assignment upon payment of a one-time fee and subject to confirmation that no third-party intellectual property is embedded. In cases where Redwood's runtime or third-party model components are involved, we will instead grant a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to the deliverable.

3) Indemnity: We propose IP infringement indemnity limited to defense costs and damages up to the liability cap; indemnity will exclude claims arising from customer data or third-party components.

Attached: Redwood_Answer_ExhibitQ_20260824.pdf (clean responses + suggested redline snippets) and the redlined Order Form (Redwood_OrderForm_Redlines_20260822.docx). If Quantico wants assignment as a firm requirement, we can provide a formal quote for the assignment fee and escalate to Legal.

Next steps: If this reflects what you need, please confirm and we will provide a contract-ready Exhibit Q. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with Legal if they prefer to walk through language.
